Classic Voices takes the voices out of Apple\'s iPhone firmware, each firmware only for its speech files. It streams just the part it needs from Apple, or reads a firmware (.ipsw) file you have. Use Wi-Fi.
Get %1$s again? It\'s already imported; this streams about %2$s.

On their own, the engines run on an emulated iPhone processor. Fast code is that same engine translated into this phone\'s own code, from your own firmware: it sounds identical and starts speaking several times sooner. Classic Voices builds it here after each firmware import: it downloads the free Zig compiler from ziglang.org (about 53 MB) and deletes it when it\'s done, and it takes a few minutes per firmware. Fast code is made from Apple\'s code, so it stays on this phone.
%1$s: fast code from an older version, slower

The text rules each voice\'s own iOS or Mac OS X release applied before speaking: “iOS” is spelled out, “OS X” is “OS ten”, St and Dr become Street and Drive, and so on.
Apple\'s later pronunciation dictionary and rules, added to the voice\'s own. Turning this on downloads them from Apple for every language (about 5 MB).

Pronunciation fixes written by Classic Voices users, for every voice of a language (github.com/nicopn/classicvoices-dicts). Turned on, Classic Voices fetches them and checks for new ones every few hours.
Apple\'s list of pronunciation rules couldn\'t be read

Enhanced and premium voices can\'t change pitch. As VoiceOver did on iOS 5 and 6, anything spoken at a changed pitch uses the voice\'s compact version. Voices without a compact version here are unaffected.
Tone as on iPhone and Mac
iPhone and Mac play the voices with their highest frequencies softened; Android keeps them, which sounds a little brighter. This softens them the same way.
Pauses keep their length at any rate
The voices shorten a pause the faster they speak, so at high rates a pause TalkBack or an app asks for almost disappears. With this on, it lasts as long at any rate.
The voices pause before, between and after spelled letters. Off, spelling is as quick as the rest of the speech. iOS 3 and 4 voices always pause.
Capital letters are spelled like small ones, without "capital" before them. TalkBack can still tell them apart its own way, if it\'s set to.
Off, Classic Voices updates to each release. On, it follows the development branch and offers every change, checking every hour when the app opens: newer, but less tested.
